s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion with electrocardiographic and echocardiographic abnormalities in a patient with a history of cardiac events and metastatic lung cancer
salient_findings: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level of 40 ng/L
ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3 on ECG
Well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum on echocardiogram
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Progressive dyspnea on exertion
History of multiple prior cardiac events
History of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium
Received 2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery 10 months prior
Denies chest pain
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level of 40 ng/L
ECG shows normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute
ECG shows ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3
ECG shows T-wave inversions in leads I, aVL, V4, V5, and V6
Echocardiogram shows well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum
Echocardiogram shows preserved left ventricular systolic function
Echocardiogram shows large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade
Coronary angiography shows nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Cardiac metastasis from lung cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium, and echocardiogram showing a well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricle

shortlist.label: Metastatic cardiac tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to cardiac metastasis, given the patient's history of lung cancer and the presence of a cardiac mass

shortlist.label: Cardiac tamponade
shortlist.why_kept: Echocardiogram showing large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade

shortlist.label: Constrictive pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of cardiac events and the presence of pericardial effusion

shortlist.label: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Preserved left ventricular systolic function and the presence of a cardiac mass, which could be causing restrictive physiology

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium, and the echocardiogram shows a well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum, which is consistent with a cardiac metastasis.

rejected.label: Metastatic cardiac tumor
rejected.why: This is essentially the same diagnosis as cardiac metastasis from lung cancer, but less specific to the patient's history of lung cancer.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: While the patient has a large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade, this is likely a consequence of the cardiac metastasis rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Constrictive pericarditis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of pericardial thickening or calcification, and the patient's symptoms and echocardiogram findings are more consistent with a cardiac metastasis.

rejected.label: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's echocardiogram shows preserved left ventricular systolic function, which is not consistent with restrictive cardiomyopathy.
